pr_title: Tag redacted document in ingest pipeline
pr_body:
Adds a new option `trace_redact` in redact processor to indicate a document has been redacted in the ingest pipeline. If a document is processed by a redact processor AND any field is redacted, ingest metadata `_ingest._redact._is_redacted = true` will be set.

Closes [#94633](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/94633)
pr_comments: Hi @samxbr, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
@samxbr just a reminder to do the backport to `8.x`

issue_context.title: [REDACT] Tag documents that have been redacted by the Redact Processor
issue_context.body:
### Description

If you want to do any kind of post-processing on documents that contain redacted data or handle documents that are redacted differently (e.g send to an alternative index) you need to test if the Redact processor has modified the document. There is no simple or convenient way to do this at the moment.

One solution is for the Redact processor to add a field such as `contains_sensitive_information: true` then another processor defined later in the ingest pipeline could run conditionally only if Redact has found something:

```
"if": "ctx.contains_sensitive_information"
# do something special with this document
```

The current workaround is to search for the string `<REDACTED>` but this will not work if the field is contains different class names such as `<EMAIL>` or `<IP_ADDRESS>`

```
"if": "ctx.message.contains('<REDACTED>')"
# do something special with this document
```

review_comments: As I'm [adding those fields to the Elasticsearch specification](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch-specification/pull/2965), I'm wondering, why do we need underscores here? Under `_ingest`, we already have `timestamp` and `pipeline` that don't use underscores.

Hi @pquentin , to my understanding, underscore is convention for ES managed/populated attributes. For example, [Grok processor](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/grok-processor.html) adds similar field `_ingest._grok_match_index` with underscore in ingest metadata.

Does it matter if it's already redacted? We only skip setting this if the metadata field is true already. It doesn't look like it can ever be false. Couldn't we just overwrite the field regardless of its existing value?

It is possible that a redact processor does not actually modify the document (the pattern is not found), in that case I think we should not set `_is_redacted` to true . 

In the case of multiple redact processors, if the first processor redacts the doc and sets `_is_redacted` to true, and the second processor does not redact the doc, we want to skip setting `_is_redacted` in the second processor to prevent overriding the previously true value.
